## Overview

LRPMM101 is the **prior-geometry sensitivity companion** to [LRPMM01](../lrp-rli-mm-001). It
is the same model, the same data and the same sampler settings, differing in exactly one
thing: the **loading / residual parameterisation**.

| | LRPMM01 (reference) | LRPMM101 (this model) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| free parameter | communality $c_j \sim \text{Beta}(2, 2)$ | $\lambda_j \sim \text{HalfNormal}(1)$, $\sigma_j \sim \text{HalfNormal}(1)$ |
| loading $\lambda_j$ | $\sqrt{c_j}$ (derived) | free |
| residual $\sigma_j$ | $\sqrt{1 - c_j}$ (derived) | free |
| $\lambda_j^2 + \sigma_j^2$ | $= 1$ exactly | unconstrained |
| everything else | — | identical, including `target_accept` = 0.999 |

Holding the sampler equal is deliberate: the geometry is the **single free variable**, so
any difference in the posterior is attributable to it and to nothing else. Both geometries
share a prior **median communality of 0.5** — the contrast isolates the *shape* of the
prior, not its central tendency.

## Why this model exists

The reference fit adopted the communality-scale parameterisation in #383: standardised
indicators have unit sample variance, so a free indicator's model-implied variance budget
is $\lambda^2 + \sigma^2 \approx 1$, and the legacy free pair ignores it. Squaring the two
independent $\text{HalfNormal}(1)$ scales gives $\chi^2_1$ variables, so the legacy pair
implies $c \sim \text{Beta}(\tfrac12, \tfrac12)$ — an **arcsine prior** that piles mass on
both singular corners (the $\lambda \to 0$ neck and the Heywood-adjacent $c \to 1$
boundary) and puts about **32 % of loading mass above 1**, which the unit budget rules out.
This companion retains that legacy pair so the geometry change stays testable rather than
asserted.

(This slot originally held the #261 "recalibrated" free pair, registered to un-confound
that revision's prior change from its measure-preserving marginalisation. The ablation —
`notes/202607101638-mm-001-convergence-reparameterisation.md` — found the recalibration
neither necessary nor sufficient for convergence while shifting prior-implied median
communality 0.50 → 0.79, a substantive commitment about exactly the quantity the model
estimates. It was rejected, and that question is settled; the live question is the
geometry.)

## Required comparison

The communality-scale and legacy-pair fits may be compared only when both current
reporting traces pass the complete automatic gate. Earlier ablation runs are diagnostic
history, not a waiver or a substitute for artefact-driven status. After a clean pair is
available, compare factor correlations, structural slopes and communalities with Monte
Carlo uncertainty; do not infer prior robustness merely because point estimates appear
similar. The indicator-scale prior-predictive check quantifies the calibration difference
directly: the legacy pair generates indicator data ~1.4× more dispersed than observed,
while the communality scale is calibrated at ~1.0 by construction.

_Measurement / triangulation, NOT causal._ As with LRPMM01: per the locked DAG's **ID-2**, every factor → gain slope is a
**latent-ability-confounded adjusted association**. The corresponding randomised-arm result
is the available-case modified ITT estimate in `lrp-rli-itt-010`; the `gain_factors`
randomised term is also outside this model.
